title: Restore and resolve routes only inside the active workspace

requirements.invariant: Navigation consumes typed route-resolution state and emits route intent without constructing provider paths, authorizing access, retaining infrastructure values, or inferring server truth from local availability.
A route can resolve from authorized cached local state without a server round trip, while not-yet-synchronized remains explicit and a stale or unavailable server does not become false absence.

Environment, Principal, Account, activation, and route scope fail closed; inaccessible, missing, unauthenticated, and revoked entity causes cannot be distinguished through the public presentation state.

Restoration and resolution are namespaced to one coherent target environment and active workspace; switching or re-entering a workspace rejects late results from the prior activation even when the route IDs match.

Deterministic provider-free fixtures prove cached restoration, context switching, cancellation-equivalent late-result rejection, not-synced state, non-enumerating failure, and contract-version refusal.

items: WorkspaceRouteScope contains exactly one Ledger target environment, PrincipalID, and AccountID; WorkspaceActivationID distinguishes successive entries into the same scope.

RouteKindID and RouteDefinition form a closed registry that validates whether a route requires a subject and which bounded parent entity kinds it may carry; raw paths, URLs, table names, document paths, and arbitrary payload dictionaries are excluded.
ScopedRoute contains one registered route kind plus only its validated stable subject and optional parent reference.
RouteRestorationRecord is contract-versioned and produces a deterministic SHA-256 key over the exact environment/Principal/Account scope and route value.

RouteResolutionRequest binds scope, activation, request identity, and route; public RouteResolutionState is closed over loading, ready, notSynced, unavailable, retryable failure, and required-update failure.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: Transient route state introduces no target relation, view, function, constraint, or index.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: The slice executes no server query or business command; owning feature query slices later resolve registered routes.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, or function is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row is introduced; owning projections remain responsible for authorization before download.

syncStreams.notApplicable: This slice represents local resolution readiness but defines no PowerSync Stream, subscription, or row visibility policy.

items: A validated restoration record is serializable and can reconstruct the same route and key without a network, but only when environment, Principal, Account, route registry, and contract version all match.

RouteResolutionReducer accepts only updates matching the active scope, activation, request identity, and route; old-account, prior-activation, old-request, and wrong-route results fail without mutating current state.

Internal missing, authorization, authentication, and revocation causes collapse to public unavailable and clear any cached destination snapshot; notSynced remains distinct and retryable infrastructure failure may retain only the explicitly supplied safe cached snapshot.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No attachment identity, byte, object, URL, or display-source behavior is introduced.

appMcp.notApplicable: This is app navigation state; MCP uses the owning typed queries and never consumes or publishes UI restoration records.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase navigation stack or transient view state is migrated.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: The shared value/reducer layer emits no telemetry; a later shell slice may record bounded route categories without entity IDs.

items: The contracts are additive target-only Swift code, import no provider SDK, alter no current app project, contact no hosted service, and activate no production behavior.
Concrete screens and feature route definitions opt in later; reverting this foundation before cutover removes only target-only code, tests, and transient target restoration values.

verification.expected: The closed route registry accepts only valid stable kinds, subject requirements, and parent scopes; restoration keys are deterministic and contain no raw identifier or provider path.
Encoding and decoding an accepted record reconstructs the same route and key offline, while environment, Principal, Account, registry, and contract-version mismatches are rejected.

Missing/unauthorized/unauthenticated/revoked updates are publicly identical and clear cached data; notSynced is distinct; prior workspace, activation, request, and route updates are rejected without changing active state.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: Immutable pull-request evidence containing the unchanged implementation passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target test suite, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent technical-control foundation derived from the app-shell capability dossier. It stops before Auth/session policy, workspace lifecycle, local database/Sync implementation, feature query ports, concrete iOS/macOS navigation, accessibility/visual evidence, hosted resources, migration, release, or cutover authority.
